app.title: Invisible Hands: V&A Collections API Research Prototype
app.summary: A person enters a search query and sets a page size, and the interface pulls matching catalogue records from a museum collections API. If the live request fails, it falls back to a small set of illustrative sample rows. The person narrows the records to a made-after and made-before year range, and can choose whether records with dates that cannot be parsed are kept. Each record is scored by how many of the catalogue fields that support follow-up are filled in. The score gives it a cautious evidence-status label, the list of fields that were found, and suggested archival follow-up routes. The person reads summary counts, the enriched record table and image thumbnails, then downloads the enriched table as CSV to decide which records deserve closer archival research.

task.text: Rank museum catalogue records by how traceable they are in archives, so a researcher can pick which ones to follow up and know where to look next.

data.text: Museum object catalogue records fetched as CSV from a collections API, one row per object with metadata fields (type, title, place, maker, maker role, date, material, technique, image id)

stage.text: first-pass triage of catalogue records before archival research

mechanism.text: Sidebar controls for the search and the date filter drive a single pipeline: fetch, filter by year, score each record by its filled fields, then add a label, reasons and next steps. Summary metrics, the enriched record table and a thumbnail grid all redraw from the result, and the table can be exported as CSV.

field.text: metadata-based archival triage of museum collections in the digital humanities

workflow.name: score records by completeness and pick which to follow up

steps.here: A search query, a page-size slider and an images-only checkbox build a CSV request to the collections API. The exact URL is shown in an expander, and a sample CSV is used if the request fails or the person asks for it.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Made-after and made-before year inputs filter on the first four-digit year parsed from the free-text date. A strict toggle decides whether records whose dates cannot be parsed are dropped.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each record scores 0 to 9, one point for each of nine catalogue fields that is filled in. The score maps to an evidence-status label, and the record gets reasons ('maker name present; ...') and rule-based archival next steps.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: Metrics show the number of records loaded, the mean score and the maximum possible score, along with counts by evidence status and the top five maker names and places.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A four-column grid shows a thumbnail for each record that has an image id, captioned with title, maker, date and a link to the object page. A slider sets how many thumbnails are shown.
A 'Download enriched CSV' button saves the displayed table with its scores, labels, reasons and next steps.

distinctive: The score measures archival tractability (how many follow-up fields are filled in), not the likelihood of the property being researched, and the interface states this caution explicitly.

Each record gets suggested archival routes based on which fields are present: prosopographical, role-term, place-based, business-archive and object-led routes, plus a separate prompt for records with little metadata.
Free-text historical dates are parsed for a year, and the strict toggle controls whether records with dates that cannot be parsed are kept.
Live API data falls back to labelled illustrative sample rows, so the workflow still runs offline.
